 Medium

 Print Detroit Red Wings' Dylan Larkin trade saga (Imagn Images) The Detroit Red Wings have taken a firm position in their growing dispute with Dylan Larkin, suspending their captain without pay after he refused to play for the team. The decision came Thursday, following Larkin's message to the club that he would not return to the ice unless Detroit traded him. What had been a difficult trade situation has now become a direct standoff between the franchise and its captain. Detroit's response also puts Larkin's immediate future in doubt. Detroit suspends Larkin as trade standoff escalates
 Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff announced the suspension hours after the dispute reached a breaking point. He also made clear that Detroit has not ended trade discussions. “Dylan Larkin has informed us that he will no longer play for the Detroit Red Wings. We are disappointed by his decision, particularly given his obligations to the organization and his teammates. We have therefore suspended Dylan without pay. “We will continue to explore trade opportunities involving Dylan. In addition to needing his approval, any trade must also be in the best interests of the Detroit Red Wings and support the organization’s long-term goals. “I want to thank and commend our coaches and players for their continued focus, and being committed to competing every day.” Larkin's full no-trade clause means he must approve any destination. Detroit will not accept a deal simply to end the dispute. His agent, Pat Brisson, defended the player's approach. “Dylan’s had enough of the situation. We believe he’s been very professional and cooperative through this process,” Brisson said. Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Larkin's camp told Detroit he had given the club enough time to act and would stay out indefinitely to force a trade. TSN put the suspension's cost at roughly $41,237.11 per day. Larkin's trade request has been months in the making
 Larkin asked to leave after the 2025-26 season. Former general manager Steve Yzerman confirmed the request in June. Minnesota, Florida and Vegas were among the original teams on the player's list, which later expanded to 10. Join conversation

 Detroit stripped Larkin of the captaincy on September 11. Horcoff became interim general manager four days later, with authority over trades. He now has to weigh Larkin's demand against the return Detroit expects. Larkin has five seasons left on an eight-year, $69.6 million contract signed in March 2023. It carries an $8.7 million average annual value and a full no-trade clause. Minnesota is among the aggressive pursuers, but no agreement has been reached. He has two goals and four assists in 10 games this season. Detroit has drawn a line: Larkin will not be paid while he refuses to play, and any trade must meet the club's terms. But the suspension does not settle the standoff. Larkin can block a destination, while Detroit can wait for an offer it values.
